To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found rare CNVs in 38% of adult patients with LGC.

1) there is a high frequency (38%) of rare CNVs among adult patients with LGC-like epilepsy; 2) the phenotypes of these syndromic disorders may be obscured in adult patients with intractable seizures; 3) a genome wide approach might shed light on these phenotypes; and 4) the CNVs identified are consistent with the clinical features of known genetic syndroms, including 2q23, 3q29, 7q11
we identified rare CNVs in 38% of the patients with LGS, which could contribute to their phenotypes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic causes in adult patients with severe epilepsy.
the genetic basis of LGS and LGS-like epilepsy in adults, with the aim of finding aetiological factors that may help to explain the phenotypes.
the identification and classification of genetic disorders, and the development of diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to improve the outcome of patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LGS is not a monogenic disease but rather a syndrome that can be caused by a variety of genetic defects, some of them still unknown.
in adult patients with severe intractable epilepsy, a genetic cause can be identified in 19% of cases, and that in 38% a genetic cause might contribute to their disease.
the etiology of LGS is complex, and a combination of genetic and non-genetic factors is probably involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CNVs identified are likely to contribute to the epilepsy phenotype.
CNVs are a significant cause of adult-onset LGS-like epilepsy and should be searched for in all such patients, regardless of age at onset.
the CNV analysis is useful in the diagnostic workup of LGS and other severe epilepsies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aCGH should be performed in adult patients with intractable seizures to identify genetic disorders that might be treatable.
